items.title: 68191_William (Bill) H. Challis Oral History Interview
items.q: INTERVIEWER: ...I drew a parallel with Stan Getz. He reminded me of Getz in this picture. ... INTERVIEWEE: I remember at the time -- what's that early tenor saxophone player Jack -- that used to play around New York.

ctx.x: The Goldkette band was a different thing. The only thing that they had and that they had set up was My Pretty Girl which is a fantastic thing anyway, and it had three trumpet, you know, Trumbauer played a great part in that, and the ensemble was good. They also had an arrangement of the --that Don Murray had made. The name doesn't come right now. But it was a fine arrangement. He was an excellent musician. Good arranger. But you couldn't get him to do anything, like a lot of guys.

I remember seeing a picture of him and he seemed like a very handsome guy, too, in fact, at the time that I saw the picture, you know, maybe 15 years ago or so, I drew a parallel with Stan Getz. He reminded me of Getz in this picture. I don't know what he looked like in real life.
I remember at the time -- what's that early tenor saxophone player Jack -- that used to play around New York.
